intro: Tickets, platforms, delays and the questions you need at a station or an airport.
p.de ida y vuelta.consejo: A ticket for going and coming back. The «y» sounds like an i: de I-da i BWEL-ta.
p.solo ida.consejo: It is a ticket without a return. Here «solo» has no accent.
p.andén.consejo: It has an accent on the é because it ends in n and the stress is at the end: an-DÉN.
p.retraso.consejo: You say «con retraso» or «de retraso»: «el tren lleva diez minutos de retraso».
p.sale.consejo: Timetables use the present: «el tren sale a las diez».
p.llega.consejo: The ll sounds y. Timetables use the present: «llega a las doce».
p.vuelo.consejo: You say «el vuelo sale» or «el vuelo llega». It comes from «volar».
p.maleta.consejo: It is feminine: «la maleta». Before travelling you say «hacer la maleta».
p.puerta de embarque.consejo: «Embarcar» comes from «barco», although today it is also used with planes.
p.facturar.consejo: At the airport you say «facturar la maleta». The c sounds k.
p.asiento.consejo: On a plane it has a number and can be by the window or the aisle.
p.tren.consejo: It has just one syllable: TREN. You take it at the station.
p.equipaje.consejo: It is masculine and usually not plural: «el equipaje». The j sounds h.
p.directo.consejo: It changes with the noun: «un tren directo», «una conexión directa».
b1.texto:
To buy: **Un billete de ida y vuelta** para Sevilla, por favor. You can also ask for **solo ida**.

To ask about the trip:

- **¿A qué hora sale** el próximo tren?
- **¿A qué hora llega?**
- **¿De qué andén sale?**
- **¿Es directo?** or **¿Hay que hacer transbordo?**

Timetables use the present: el tren **sale** a las diez and **llega** a las doce. A late train **lleva** veinte minutos **de retraso**.

At the airport you **facturas** the suitcase, look for the **puerta de embarque** and check whether the **vuelo** is cancelled. **Directo** agrees with the noun: un tren directo, una conexión directa.
b2.f0.texto: I want a return ticket to Seville, please.
b2.f1.texto: The next train leaves at ten.
b2.f2.texto: What time does it arrive in Seville?
b2.f3.texto: It arrives at half past twelve.
b2.f4.texto: Which platform does the train leave from?
b2.f7.texto: Today it is ten minutes late.
b4.texto:
Timetables and notices use the **present**, even when they speak of the future:

- El tren **sale** a las diez and **llega** a las doce.
- El vuelo **sale** de la puerta ocho.
- El viaje **tarda** dos horas.

To ask: **¿A qué hora** sale? **¿De qué andén** sale? **¿Cuánto** tarda? **¿Es** directo?

Say the delay with **lleva** or **tiene** + time + **de retraso**: el tren **lleva** veinte minutos **de retraso**.

The adjective **directo** changes with the noun: **tren directo**, **vuelo directo**, **conexión directa**.
b4.e1.texto: I check in my suitcase at the airport.
b4.e2.texto: My seat is next to the window.
b5.f0.texto: The train waits on the platform with its doors open.
b5.f1.texto: A clear mist covers the tracks and the roofs.
b5.f2.texto: The travellers drag their suitcases with a dull noise.
b5.f3.texto: A loudspeaker repeats the names of the faraway cities.
b5.f4.texto: Lucía squeezes her ticket and looks at the big clock.
b5.f5.texto: The train slowly leaves the grey station.
b5.f6.texto: The yellow fields pass by the window under the sun.
b5.f7.texto: An old woman knits a blue jumper in the next seat.
b5.f8.texto: Lucía rests her head against the cool glass and closes her eyes.
b5.f9.texto: The rattling of the train gently carries her towards sleep.
b6.o0.refuerzo: That's it! «Ida y vuelta» is going and coming back.
b6.o1.refuerzo: «Vuelto» is change in money in some countries.
b6.o2.refuerzo: «Volver» is a verb; a noun is needed here.
b7.o0: El tren va veinte minutos tarde
b7.o0.refuerzo: Yes! A delay is extra waiting time.
b7.o1: El tren sale en veinte minutos
b7.o1.refuerzo: That would be the departure time, not a delay.
b7.pregunta: The board says «retraso: 20 min». What does it mean?
b8.frase: De qué andén sale el tren
b8.traduccion: Which platform does the train leave from
b9.o0.refuerzo: Well done: «sale» is the moment of departure.
b9.o1.refuerzo: «Llega» is the end of the trip, not the start.
b10.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «What time does the train leave?»
b11.o0.refuerzo: Facturar is not buying; it is handing it over at the airport.
b11.o1.refuerzo: Exactly! It travels on the plane without you carrying it.
b11.o2.refuerzo: Opening the suitcase is another action.
b12.o2.refuerzo: «Directos» is plural; there is only one train.
b12.pregunta: Choose the form that agrees with «tren».
p.facturo.consejo: From «facturar», to check in luggage. The stress is on TU.
p.neblina.consejo: The stress falls on BLI. The b sounds soft.
p.altavoz.consejo: The z at the end sounds like «th» in Spain.
p.teje.consejo: From «tejer», to knit. The j sounds like h.
p.contra.consejo: Means «against» or «leaning on». Not the same as «contrario».
p.traqueteo.consejo: The stress is on TE. The «eo» at the end is two separate syllables.
p.ida.consejo: Feminine noun. «Billete de ida» is a one-way ticket.
p.entregarla.consejo: From «entregar» with «la» at the end: to hand it over.
p.avión.consejo: The tilde on the ó shows the stress is on the last syllable.
